solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boosts for mobility aids

blocks.note: first meaning: helping hands that lift someone onward
second meaning, read whimsically: limbs that are raised, the things that let us walk

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: legs are the body's own mobility aids, and the answer splits into those plus a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a helping start or boost in life or career is the common idiomatic sense of the hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Broadcast listener received in part of Ireland

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio programme picked up by someone tuning in somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture so well that it hides its job as the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, the eastern one containing Dublin.

clue.text: Picturesque caves where little piggies are under filth

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming after it in the column

blocks.note: grot is British slang for dirt or rubbish
from the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy', counted on a child's toes

explanation.surface: A pastoral scene of piglets wallowing in muck in a pretty cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy went to market' is a toe-counting nursery rhyme, so piggies are toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, often ornamental or attractive, kept for its scenic charm.

clue.text: Falsely claims before nurses

blocks.note: the prefix meaning before
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone making false allegations ahead of the nursing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' reads as a preposition about time but simply supplies its Latin-derived prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make a false assertion, profess something untrue, or put on a deceptive show.

clue.text: Stomach complaint from police department in oasis, floundering

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters stumble into disorder
one thing set inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A detective unit lost in the desert picks up a tummy bug at a water hole.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidosis is excess acidity in the body's fluids; loosely, an acid stomach, the kind of digestive upset the clue names.

clue.text: Singing in bath ultimately in the pink

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a singing group

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept
one thing placed inside another

blocks.note: its last letter
coral is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: Someone happily belting out songs in the tub, feeling in the pink of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' is an idiom for healthy, which hides that 'the pink' is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music performed by a choir or group of voices, as in a singing ensemble.

clue.text: Germany’s empire is dismal

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
the German word for empire

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict on German imperial history.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Scots word, used across Britain for grey, drizzly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreich is Scottish dialect for bleak, dreary and gloomy, especially describing wet overcast weather.

clue.text: Took possession of Devizes, laid waste, five missing

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so it must be taken out
a place laid waste is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An invading army captures a Wiltshire market town and razes it, losing five men.
explanation.walkthrough: Devizes is a market town in Wiltshire, England; remove its V, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to grab or capture forcibly, taking control or ownership of something.

clue.text: Highlight singular hair

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser putting a single highlight in a client's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' suggests hair colouring, but here it is a verb meaning to emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, giving it special prominence or attention.

clue.text: Pressed on — ride off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider pushing on before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed on' reads as a phrase meaning continued, but the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes means smoothing them with a hot iron, so pressed garments have been flattened that way.

clue.text: More desperate for company, lecturer removed touch of naughtiness from joke

indicators.note: a touch is a tiny trace, so only the first letter is taken
something removed is taken away, so it comes out of the word

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer
a one-liner is a short joke
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lecturer, wanting to be liked, cleans up a smutty joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke loses its first N, leaving ONELIER, and the lecturer's L goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonelier is the comparative of lonely, describing someone craving more companionship and friendship.

clue.text: Wild street dog

indicators.note: wild means unruly and uncontrolled, so the letters run free

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A feral stray roaming the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a stray, but the answer is a gun-dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gundog, such as the Irish or English setter, trained to point at game.

clue.text: The class destroyed their bags

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly schoolroom wrecks its own school bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the answer: schoolchildren carry these.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag with a shoulder strap, traditionally carried by schoolchildren for books.

clue.text: Spell of finess regularly producing my own photos

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A spell of cleverness yields a batch of self-portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finess' is a deliberate misspelling of finesse to make the alternate letters work; 'Spell' is part of the fodder, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph you take of yourself, usually at arm's length with a phone camera.

clue.text: Some of the elvers — only this one is adult

indicators.note: some of means a portion, so the answer is a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Among a shoal of baby fish, just one has grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvers are young eels, so the grown-up version of them is the hidden fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a juvenile, and the mature creature it grows into is a snake-like fish.

clue.text: Stops ringing me, which improves things

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to stop is to end
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stops phoning me, and life gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' fits the telephone picture, but it means circling.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or revise, typically a text, removing errors so it reads better.

clue.text: Go mad as result of committing serious foul?

blocks.note: first meaning: lose one's temper
second meaning: a footballer shown the red card for a bad foul is sent off

explanation.walkthrough: In football, a serious foul gets the player a red card from the referee; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become suddenly furious, while literally a sent-off player is shown the red card.

clue.text: Fly catcher seen in WWW

blocks.note: first meaning: a spider's net for trapping insects
second meaning: the third W of the internet's initials stands for it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly catcher' sounds like a bird, the flycatcher, but it is the spider's trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins a silken net to snare insects, and the internet's World Wide Web borrows the same word.

clue.text: Coastal wet mist in Kent and Sussex after being unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both counties lie in England's South East, abbreviated SE
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather report on sea mist rolling into south-eastern England after a stormy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word linking parts, but it is the anagram fodder. Kent and Sussex are counties in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold fog drifting inland from the sea, a term used on England's eastern coasts.

clue.text: Wing and tail feathers missing one short month

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: a peacock's long tail feathers are its train
I is the Roman numeral for one
the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: A bird moulting its wing and tail feathers for a few weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' suggests birds, matching the feathers, but it means an arm of a cross-shaped church.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cruciform church, a side wing crossing the nave at right angles.

clue.text: Crazy, like a door hanging loose

blocks.note: first meaning: mentally unbalanced
second meaning: literally off its hinges

explanation.walkthrough: The figurative sense of mental instability comes straight from the image of a door off its fixings.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhinged means mentally deranged, and literally describes something detached from the pivots it swings on.

clue.text: Lectern reconstructed at start of year, just a few weeks ago

indicators.note: the start is the beginning, so only the opening letter is used
reconstructed means rebuilt differently, so the letters form a new word

blocks.note: taken as written
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A church reading desk was rebuilt in January, only weeks back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y joins the lectern's letters before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means in the near past, a short time before now, such as a matter of weeks.

clue.text: Medal for England’s Lucy

blocks.note: first meaning: the third-place award
second meaning: the surname of a famous England women's football defender

explanation.walkthrough: Lucy Bronze is a star defender for England's women's football team, winner of the Euros.
explanation.definitionFit: Third place earns a medal of this metal, and it is also the surname of the England footballer.

clue.text: Orban’s successor with small monthly tale cut short

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a mag is a magazine, the word shortened
a yarn is a long story

explanation.surface: A new Hungarian leader takes office alongside a brief magazine story.
explanation.walkthrough: Péter Magyar replaced Viktor Orbán as Hungary's prime minister in 2026; the word also means Hungarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Péter Magyar's Tisza party defeated Viktor Orbán in Hungary's 2026 election, making him the next prime minister.

clue.text: Weapon from Knight of the Round Table — look out!

indicators.note: out means taken away or excluded, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: Sir Lancelot, Arthur's foremost knight
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A warning cry as an Arthurian knight swings his weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look out!' reads as a warning shout, but splits into a word for look and a removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a small double-edged surgical blade, and historically also a small lance.

clue.text: Get on with this, you understand?

definitions.text: Get on with this, you understand?

blocks.note: surface reading: an order to carry on with a task
setter's reading: add 'on' to the answer and you get a phrase meaning to grasp or catch on

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an impatient instruction; in fact putting 'on' after the answer forms an idiom for understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The British phrasal verb pairing this word with 'on' means to come to understand or realise something.

clue.text: See 15
Paper money turned up for eating apple

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up flips it to read bottom to top

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Banknotes offered in exchange for a dessert apple.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note. Rennet is more familiar as a cheese-making enzyme; here it is an old apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet (or reinette) is an old variety of dessert apple, a type grown for eating raw.

clue.text: Fishes sailor’s caught all by himself

definitions.note: the answer is shellfish, a noun plural, loosely called fishes

indicators.note: to catch is to hold, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, plus the possessive S
being all by oneself is being alone

explanation.surface: A lone seaman reels in a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishes' looks like a verb about angling, but it is a plural noun for the sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone are edible sea snails, molluscs loosely grouped with seafood and fish in everyday speech.

clue.text: Individual around cypress, say, ablaze

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: one means a single individual
'say' marks an example: cypress and fir are both conifers

explanation.surface: Someone standing by a burning tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that the tree is standing in for a fellow conifer rather than being taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze and burning both describe something alight with flames, the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Sailing around cay before night out

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
out means disordered or not right, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written; a cay is a small low island
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cruising round a tropical islet before an evening ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts the first piece in front; 'around' tempts as a container signal but here it turns the island back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachting is the sport or pastime of sailing in yachts, racing or cruising for pleasure.

clue.text: Oppressiveness of the wig abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so the letters are let loose

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge gladly casting off a stifling wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as discarded, but its sense of wild and unrestrained is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight on the mind is a burden; heaviness and pressure convey the same oppressive sense.

clue.text: Head over after liturgy’s slow passage

blocks.note: a rite is a liturgical ceremony; the 's links it on
nut is slang for head
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cleric looks up after a slow reading from the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the first two pieces behind RITE. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, written O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is an Italian musical direction marking a section to be played with an immediate slowing of tempo.

clue.text: Heavy messy dog in messy place

indicators.note: messy means untidy and jumbled, so the letters are muddled
one thing set inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a pigsty is the byword for a filthy place

explanation.surface: A big, filthy dog lounging in a squalid room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' appears twice: first as the shuffle signal, then as part of the description of a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is heavy and filling, and the word extends to dull, weighty prose or people.
